The graph of the cubic function f(x)=ax3+bx2+cx+d is shown below.

A turning point is located at (2,0) and the shaded region shown on the graph has an area of 16units2.

Use the above information to determine the values of a,b,candd.
answerHtml:
Supplied worked solution and marking criteria

The graph of the cubic function f(x)=ax3+bx2+cx+d is shown below.

A turning point is located at (2,0) and the shaded region shown on the graph has an area of 16units2.

Use the above information to determine the values of a,b,candd.

Solution

Firstly, note that

f′(x)=3ax2+2bx+c

and

f″(x)=6ax+2b

Given that there is an inflection point at x=12 , it follows that f″(12)=0.Hence,

3a+2b=0⇒b=−−3a2

Given that there is a turning point at x=2 , it follows that f′(2)=0.Hence,

12a+4b+c=0⇒c=−6a

Given that there is an x-intercept at x=2 , it follows that f(2)=0.Hence,

8a+4b+2c+d=0⇒d=10a

Finally, given that the area of the shaded region is 16 , it follows that ∫02f(x)dx=−16.

a∫02(x3−32x2−6x+10)dx=−16

a[x44−3x36−6x22+10x]02=−16

8a=−16⇒a=−2

Hence, a=−2,b=3,c=12,d=−20

Or

Solving 4 equations using classpad
Specific behaviours

ü recognises f″(12)=0 and hence that b=−−3a2

ü recognises f′(2)=0 and hence that c=−6a

ü recognises f(2)=0 and hence that d=10a

ü recognises ∫02f(x)dx=−16

ü evaluates definite integral to determine that a=−2

ü solves for the values of b,candd.

html:
Faultings is a hardware store that sells discounted hardware.

In the electrical section they have a large box containing many light globes. The box has a sign with the text ‘Super Sale! 40% of these light globes are faulty’.

(a) A customer picks a light globe at random and records whether it is faulty or not. Explain why this is a Bernoulli experiment. (2 marks)

(b) Determine the mean and standard deviation for the Bernoulli experiment in part (a).

(2 marks)

A customer needs six working light globes. Based on the sign they buy 10 light globes.

(c) Assuming the sign is correct,

(i) State the distribution that models the number of working globes. (2 marks)

(ii) Determine the mean and variance for the distribution in part (c)(i). (2 marks)

(iii) Assuming the sign is correct, determine the probability that out of the 10 globes
bought, at least six are working. (1 mark)

A second customer needs eight working light globes for a light fitting in their stairwell.

(d) This customer buys 12 light globes, and tests them one-by-one. They will stop when they have exactly eight working globes.

Assuming 40% of the globes are faulty, determine the probability they will need to test all 12 globes. (3 marks)

Another customer believes only 30% of the globes are working. If there is at least k working globes then Faultings is right, and if the number of working globes is less than k then the customer is right.

(e) The customer takes a sample of 50 bulbs. Using k=20, determine the probability

(i) Faultings is correct in saying 40% of the globes are faulty. (1 mark)

(ii) the customer is correct in saying 30% of the globes are working. (2 marks)

A customer needs six working light globes. Based on the sign they buy 10 light globes.

(c) Assuming the sign is correct,

(i) State the distribution that models the number of working globes. (2 marks)

Pr(X≥6)=0.6331

A second customer needs eight working light globes for a light fitting in their stairwell.

(d) This customer buys 12 light globes, and tests them one-by-one. They will stop when they have exactly eight working globes.

Assuming 40% of the globes are faulty, determine the probability they will need to test all 12 globes. (3 marks)

Solution

Pr(Y=7)=0.236490

Pr(needtotestall12)

=0.236490×0.6=0.1419

Another customer believes only 30% of the globes are working. If there is at least k working globes then Faultings is right, and if the number of working globes is less than k then the customer is right.

(i) Faultings is correct in saying 40% of the globes are faulty. (1 mark)

Solution

Pr(YFaultings≥20)=0.9986
Specific behaviours

  • Determines probability.

(ii) the customer is correct in saying 30% of the globes are working. (2 marks)

Solution

YCustomer∼Bin(50,0.3)

Pr(YCustomer<20)=0.9152

html:
During early 2024 a survey was conducted by a university on the ‘2 Fruit & 5 Veg’ campaign. Participants in the survey were asked if they ate at least 1 piece of fruit and at least 4 vegetables each day.

From the 227 participants, 134 said they ate at least 1 piece of fruit and at least 4 vegetables each day.

  1. What feature of this sample indicates that a normal distribution can be used to model the sample proportion of supportive people? (1 mark)

(b) On the basis of this sample, determine a point estimate for p. (1 mark)

(c) Determine a 95% confidence interval for p. (2 marks)

(d) Does this sample provide evidence that the proportion of people who support the ban has changed from an earlier figure of 62%? Justify your answer. (2 marks)

(e) The university also considered calculating a 90% confidence interval. Determine the minimum sample size to ensure that the margin of error of a 90% confidence interval for p is at most 0.025. (3 marks)

The participants in the survey were recommended by a local hospital, and they had to keep a diary of the food they ate for a week.

(f) Identify and explain a potential source of bias in this sampling method. (2 marks)
answerHtml:
Supplied worked solution and marking criteria

During early 2024 a survey was conducted by a university on the ‘2 Fruit & 5 Veg’ campaign. Participants in the survey were asked if they ate at least 1 piece of fruit and at least 4 vegetables each day.

From the 227 participants, 134 said they ate at least 1 piece of fruit and at least 4 vegetables each day.

  1. What feature of this sample indicates that a normal distribution can be used to model the sample proportion of supportive people? (1 mark)

(b) On the basis of this sample, determine a point estimate for p. (1 mark)

Solution
134227≈0.59
Specific behaviours

  • Correctly calculates point estimate.

(c) Determine a 95% confidence interval for p. (2 marks)

Solution
0.5263≤p≤0.6543
Specific behaviours

  • Uses correct critical value.

  • Calculates correct confidence interval

(allow 3 decimal places but WACE will want 4 dp)

(d) Does this sample provide evidence that the proportion of people who support the ban has changed from an earlier figure of 62%? Justify your answer. (2 marks)

(e) The university also considered calculating a 90% confidence interval. Determine the minimum sample size to ensure that the margin of error of a 90% confidence interval for p is at most 0.025. (3 marks)

Solution

0.025=1.6450.5×(1−0.50n

n=1083
Specific behaviours

  • Uses p=0.5.

  • forms correct equation for n using z = 1.645 (minimum accuracy)

  • Determines correct sample size and rounds up

The participants in the survey were recommended by a local hospital, and they had to keep a diary of the food they ate for a week.

(f) Identify and explain a potential source of bias in this sampling method. (2 marks)

Solution

Many possible answers, for example:

Location bias: the participants were sourced from a ‘local hospital’ which is not reflective of the whole population as not every individual from the population will access the same hospital facility and service.

Time bias: the journalling is limited to one week and the amount of fruit and vegetables consumed per week can fluctuate from any other week due to lifestyle changes (e.g. diet), financial circumstances etc.

Selection bias: the hospital may have sent people who needed to improve their diet (sample is not random).

Recording bias: people may have inflated the number of fruit and vegetables eaten as it was being recorded.
Specific behaviours

  • Identifies a source of bias.

  • Explains how the source introduces bias.

Answers should be specific to this situation, avoid generic answers that are vague and not specific to the actual question.

html:
A radio station was producing a story based on a 2011 study into zoonotic infections which found that 45% of cat owners in Australia allowed their cat to jump onto their kitchen sink.

In order to check whether this proportion had changed since the original study, a researcher from the station planned to collect a new data sample by standing at the entrance to a local train station one afternoon and asking all commuters who pass by.

(a) Identify and explain two sources of bias in the researcher's sampling method. (4 marks)

The radio station decided to contract the research to a professional company, who asked the question to a random sample of 240 Australian cat owners.

(b) Assuming that the 2011 proportion was correct,

(i) determine the probability that less than 102 of the owners sampled allowed their cat to jump onto their kitchen sink. (3 marks)

(ii) determine, using the approximate normality of the distribution, the probability that the sample proportion of owners who allow their cat to jump onto their kitchen sink will be less than 0.425. (3 marks)

In the original 2011 study, the confidence interval for the proportion of pet owners who allowed their dog to share their bed was (0.2019,0.3759), based on a sample of 180 owners.

(c) Determine the number of pet owners in the sample who allowed their dog to share their bed. (2 marks)

(d) Determine the level of confidence that was used to calculate the confidence interval.

(3 marks)
